Index.meta_title: SaaS SolidJS - Build and scale multi-tenant SaaS with SolidStart
Index.meta_description: Production-ready SolidStart starter with auth, organizations, Stripe billing, Resend email, and English/Chinese i18n.

Hero.title: The perfect <important>SaaS SolidJS</important> starter to build and scale your business with ease.
Hero.description: Auth, organizations, Stripe subscriptions, and Resend email — a SolidStart foundation ready for production.

Features.section_title: Everything you need to ship SaaS
Features.section_description: Multi-tenant building blocks wired for real customers — not just a demo shell.
Features.feature1_description: Email/password sessions, verification, and password reset with hashed tokens.
Features.feature2_description: Invite members, assign admin/member roles, and keep tenants isolated.
Features.feature3_description: Checkout, Customer Portal, and webhooks that sync subscription status.
Features.feature4_description: Resend-powered invites, verification, and reset flows with en/zh templates.
Features.feature5_description: SSR-aware locale switching with dictionaries for marketing and dashboard.
Features.feature6_description: Typed schema, migrations, and PGLite for local development without Docker.

Pricing.section_description: Start free. Upgrade when you need more seats and capacity.

FAQ.section_description: What teams usually ask before adopting this starter.
FAQ.a1: Yes — Postgres-backed auth, organization RBAC, Stripe subscriptions, Resend email, CSRF protection, and rate limiting are included.
FAQ.a2: No. Run PGLite with npm run db-server, or point DATABASE_URL at Neon/Postgres.
FAQ.a3: Admins start Checkout from Pricing or Billing. Stripe webhooks update your subscriptions table; Customer Portal handles upgrades and cancellations.
FAQ.a4: Yes. Admins invite by email, members accept via a secure token link, and you can resend or revoke pending invites.
FAQ.a5: English and Chinese out of the box. Locale follows cookie/SSR and maps into email and Stripe Checkout where possible.
FAQ.q6: Can I replace the auth system later?
FAQ.a6: The session layer is self-contained. You can keep it, or swap providers later without rewriting org and billing modules.
